content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 16-17. Supplemental: C4 context and container diagrams. This unit focuses on cohesion, coupling, and functional boundaries.
Functional decomposition is architectural because it shapes how the system changes. High cohesion keeps related behavior together. Low coupling reduces the number of elements affected by a change.

Boundaries should follow domain meaning, operational ownership, data consistency needs, security requirements, and team structure. A clean-looking diagram can still hide poor boundaries if responsibilities are split unnaturally.
Studio: critique a service decomposition by identifying one high-coupling dependency and one misplaced responsibility.

concepts.name: Functional cohesion
concepts.description: The degree to which responsibilities within an element belong together.

concepts.name: Functional coupling
concepts.description: The degree of dependency between functional elements.

concepts.name: Functional boundary
concepts.description: A division between responsibilities that affects ownership, change, interfaces, and runtime collaboration.

concepts.name: Responsibility leakage
concepts.description: A design problem where behavior crosses boundaries in ways that weaken cohesion or ownership.
